patients.summary: Office administrator in Amherst with hypertension, type 2 diabetes, hyperlipidemia and coronary disease who joined in 2017. Whipple disease in 2020, then stable angina on medical therapy, gout, a VT arrest-level event with ICD, acute mitral regurgitation repaired, a subdural hematoma evacuated, and a late MI with shock liver in 2025. Sparse outside records.

documents.title: New patient intake call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller is looking for a new primary care doctor; his previous physician retired this spring. Explained the membership and that labs, imaging and specialists still go through his PPO. He is on four daily medications and says he has "sugar, pressure, cholesterol and a heart thing." Booked new patient visit 6/14 at 8:40, fasting labs same morning. Records release form emailed for the old practice.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
53M here to establish. Prior PCP retired; records requested.

PMH: HTN about 8 yrs. T2DM about 6 yrs, always on metformin alone, never on insulin. High cholesterol. Coronary disease: had a stress test in 2015 that was "borderline" and then a cath at an outside hospital, told he had some plaque but nothing that needed a stent. Kept on metoprolol and atorvastatin since. No chest pain now; walks the dog most evenings without trouble.
PSH: diagnostic cardiac cath 2015. No operations.
Meds: metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 40, metoprolol succinate 50. Says he tried a higher metoprolol dose once and felt washed out, so went back to 50.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: father had a heart attack at 62. Mother with type 2 diabetes. One brother on BP pills.
SH: married, office administrator for a property management company. Never smoked. 2-3 drinks on weekends, none weekdays. No other substances.

ROS: no chest pain, dyspnea, palpitations, edema. No polyuria. No numbness in the feet. GI normal. Joints fine.

Exam: well, pleasant. BP 134/82. BMI about 29. HEENT normal. Neck supple, no bruit, no nodes. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Ext: no edema, pedal pulses 2+. Monofilament intact both feet, skin intact, no calluses.

A/P:
1. HTN: at goal-ish on lisinopril. Continue.
2. T2DM: A1c, BMP, urine microalbumin today. Continue metformin. Eye exam due; he has an optometrist in town.
3. HLD / CAD, nonobstructive per his account: continue atorva 40 and metoprolol. Will review cath report when records come.
4. Health maintenance: says colonoscopy at 50 was clean. Hep C and HIV screening offered and done today. Flu shot in the fall.
RTC 6 months, sooner as needed. Gave him the practice cell for texts.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Kurt, labs from Wednesday are back. A1c 7.8, which is reasonable and fine to keep working on with diet and walking. Kidney function and potassium normal. LDL is under 100 on the atorvastatin. Urine protein screen normal. Hep C and HIV screens negative. No changes for now.

- Cardiac catheterization 2015 at a regional hospital after an equivocal exercise test: mild nonobstructive coronary artery disease, no lesion requiring intervention. Medical therapy recommended.
- Screening colonoscopy 2014: normal to the cecum, no polyps, repeat in 10 years.
- Medication list matches what patient reported.
- A1c values 2014-2016 ranged roughly 7.0-7.6.
Scanned to media. Reviewed by PCP.

documents.title: Diarrhea and weight loss
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Texted last week about his stomach; booked in.
Since around November: crampy belly pain that comes and goes, and loose stools most days. Stools are bulky, greasy-looking, hard to flush, smell much worse than usual. No blood, no black stools. No fever. Appetite ok but he has lost weight without trying (scale here is about 10 lb under his usual). Also achy joints over the same stretch: knees, then wrists, then shoulders, moving around; never swollen or red. Taking ibuprofen 400 mg here and there for the joints, which helps some. No new meds, no travel, no antibiotics. Metformin dose unchanged for years.
Exam: thinner in the face. BP/HR as charted, afebrile. Abd soft, nondistended, mildly tender diffusely without guarding, no mass, normal bowel sounds. Joints: full range, no effusion or warmth at knees, wrists or shoulders.
A1c 7.4.
A/P: chronic steatorrhea-type diarrhea with weight loss and migratory arthralgias. Needs GI evaluation, probably scope. Referral placed, marked soon. Ok to keep ibuprofen as needed for now, with food. Recheck weight at next visit. Call if blood in stool or fevers.

documents.title: GI appointment postponed

documents.body: The GI office called to cancel my April appointment because of the virus. They put me on a list for May. Still the same with my stomach, not worse. Is that ok to wait?

documents.title: Re: GI appointment postponed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Ok to wait as long as things aren't getting worse. If you see blood, run a fever, or keep losing weight quickly, let me know and I'll push them. Stay well.

events.reason: Chronic diarrhea, abdominal pain, weight loss

reports.text: Specimen: small bowel (duodenal) mucosal biopsies, multiple fragments. Microscopic: the lamina propria contains numerous foamy macrophages. The macrophage cytoplasm is strongly positive on periodic acid-Schiff stain with diastase resistance. No granulomas. No dysplasia or malignancy.
reports.conclusion: Duodenal mucosa with PAS-positive macrophages in the lamina propria, consistent with Whipple disease in the clinical setting.

documents.title: Gastroenterology consultation and endoscopy
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Thank you for referring Mr. Levine, 56, seen 05/08/2020.

He describes half a year of on-and-off abdominal pain with chronic diarrhea that is bulky, oily and foul-smelling, and about 15 pounds of weight loss. He also has wandering joint pain affecting knees, wrists and shoulders, with no swelling or redness that he has noticed. Background: hypertension, type 2 diabetes, hyperlipidemia, nonobstructive coronary disease on medical therapy. Medications: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 20 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, metoprolol succinate 50 mg, ibuprofen 400 mg as needed. NKDA. Never smoker; drinks socially on weekends.

Exam: afebrile, BP 130/85. Generalized nontender lymphadenopathy. Abdomen soft.

Labs: Hgb 12.1, WBC 7.0, platelets 250, fasting glucose 160, albumin 3.2, ESR 50. Tissue transglutaminase antibody negative.

EGD same day: biopsies of the small bowel taken. Pathology (05/12): periodic acid-Schiff positive macrophages in the lamina propria.

Impression: Whipple disease, with malabsorption, weight loss, arthralgias and lymphadenopathy.

Plan:
1. Ceftriaxone 2 g IV once daily for 14 days. Home infusion arranged; PICC placement Monday 05/11.
2. Then trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole DS one tablet twice daily for 12 months. We will send the prescription.
3. Weekly CBC/BMP while on IV therapy through the infusion company.
4. GI follow-up in about a year with repeat endoscopy and biopsies.
Please continue his other care. Contact our office with questions.

Day 10 of IV ceftriaxone through the PICC, infusion nurse comes weekly. Already a little less diarrhea. No rash, no fever, arm with the line looks fine on camera.
Next step is the oral antibiotic for a year once the IV course ends on the 24th. Will keep an eye on his potassium and kidney function with the Bactrim plus lisinopril.
Working from home. Wife is helping with the infusions schedule. Questions answered.

documents.title: Follow-up, new exertional chest pressure
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Bowels much better on the Bactrim, formed stools most days, eating well, weight up a little. Joints quieter.

New: about 6 weeks of a pressure in the middle of his chest when he walks the hill on his street or carries groceries up from the car. Goes away within a few minutes of stopping. No radiation, no sweats, none at rest or at night. No palpitations, no syncope. Has not tried anything for it.

Exam: BP/HR as charted. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. No edema.
ECG in office: sinus, normal, no ischemic changes.

A/P:
1. Exertional chest pressure in a man with known nonobstructive CAD, diabetes, HTN, family history: sounds like angina. Cardiology referral, urgent slot requested. Continue metoprolol and atorvastatin. If it comes on at rest or doesn't settle with stopping, call 911.
2. Whipple disease on TMP-SMX: improving. Labs today.
3. T2DM: A1c 7.8, a bit up while he's been sick. No change today.
Follow-up after cardiology.

conditions.label: Angina pectoris
conditions.note: Stable angina; 70% LAD stenosis; medical management by patient preference

reports.text: Standard Bruce protocol. Resting ECG sinus rhythm without ST abnormality. Exercised to a high workload and stopped for chest pressure and fatigue. At peak exercise, horizontal ST-segment depression developed in the anterior leads, resolving in recovery. No arrhythmia. Blood pressure response appropriate.
reports.conclusion: Positive for ischemia: anterior ST depression at a high workload, with typical chest pressure.

documents.title: Cardiology consultation
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Re: Kurt Levine. Seen 09/10/2020.
Three months of worsening central chest pressure on inclines, relieved by rest. Hx nonobstructive CAD (cath 2015), HTN, T2DM, HLD; recently treated for Whipple disease, on TMP-SMX. Meds: metformin, lisinopril, atorvastatin, metoprolol succinate 50 mg, ibuprofen PRN. NKDA. FH: father MI at 62.
BP 138/86, HR 78. Exam unremarkable.
Exercise test same day: anterior ST depression at high workload, reproducing his pressure.
Coronary angiography 09/17/2020 (right radial): 70% stenosis of the left anterior descending artery; no other significant lesions.
Assessment: stable angina due to coronary artery disease.
Plan: We discussed revascularization versus medical therapy. He is hesitant about a stent and prefers to try medications; this is a reasonable approach for stable symptoms. Metoprolol succinate 50 mg is his tolerated dose (fatigue on higher doses previously). Continue atorvastatin 40 mg. Return in 6 months or sooner if symptoms worsen.

documents.title: Rheumatology consultation
documents.author: rheumatology

Urgent visit 10/25/2021, right knee.
Two days of severe right knee pain and swelling, worse with movement, red and warm. Denies trauma or insect bite. Similar but milder episodes over the past year settled with NSAIDs. PMH: HTN, T2DM, HLD, CAD with stable angina (medical management), Whipple disease treated 2020-21. Meds: metformin, lisinopril, atorvastatin, metoprolol, ibuprofen PRN. NKDA.
Exam: swollen, erythematous, tender prepatellar region of the right knee, ROM limited by pain. Bursal aspiration: yellowish fluid with white flecks.
Fluid WBC 18,000/µL, 90% PMNs. Serum uric acid 9.2, ESR 50, CRP 25.
Right knee radiographs: punched-out erosions with overhanging cortical edges.
Assessment: gout with prepatellar bursitis; chronic changes on film.
Plan: colchicine 0.6 mg twice daily until the flare settles. Return in 4 weeks to begin urate-lowering therapy.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
ED visit 11/02/2022, regional hospital.
CC: sudden palpitations with chest pressure, lightheadedness and shortness of breath.
Hx: abrupt onset at work. Substernal pressure, no radiation. Known CAD with stable angina followed by cardiology. Meds per list: metformin, lisinopril, atorvastatin, metoprolol succinate, allopurinol, ibuprofen PRN. NKDA.
VS: BP 85/50, HR 180, RR 22, SpO2 92% RA.
Exam: JVP elevated; crackles at both bases.
ECG: wide-complex tachycardia, no P waves seen.
Labs: Na 140, K 4.2, Cr 1.1, troponin I elevated.
Course: IV access, O2. Unstable; procedural sedation and synchronized cardioversion to sinus rhythm. Admitted to cardiology.
Dx: unstable wide-complex tachycardia, likely VT.

reports.text: Left ventricle normal in size. LVEF 55% by biplane Simpson. No regional wall motion abnormality. Right ventricle normal in size and function. Mitral, aortic, tricuspid and pulmonic valves structurally normal without significant regurgitation or stenosis. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: Normal LV size and systolic function, LVEF 55%. No wall motion abnormality. Normal valves.

documents.title: Discharge summary
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:

59M with CAD (stable angina, medical therapy), VT s/p ICD 2022, HTN, DM. Became short of breath and had chest discomfort walking to the grocery store; rapidly worse over an hour. Lightheaded, cannot lie flat. No known valve disease.
VS: BP 98/60, HR 112, RR 28.
Exam: diaphoretic, anxious. JVD to the angle of the mandible sitting up. New soft blowing holosystolic murmur at the apex radiating to the axilla. Bibasilar crackles. No peripheral edema.
CXR: bilateral infiltrates, enlarged left atrium. ECG: sinus tachycardia, no ST elevation or depression.
Tx: supplemental O2, IV furosemide. Pulmonary artery catheter placed for hemodynamic monitoring. Echo ordered. Cardiology and cardiac surgery consulted; admitted to CCU.
Impression: acute mitral regurgitation with pulmonary edema.

reports.text: LV normal in size, hyperdynamic. LVEF 65% by biplane Simpson. Flail posterior mitral leaflet with ruptured chordae. Severe mitral regurgitation, eccentric jet. Left atrium enlarged. RV normal size and function. Aortic valve normal. Device lead in the right heart. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: Severe mitral regurgitation due to flail posterior leaflet with ruptured chordae. LVEF 65%.

Discharge meds: home regimen unchanged.
Follow-up: cardiac surgery 2 weeks, cardiology 6 weeks. Sternal precautions 6-8 weeks.

documents.title: Discharge summary
documents.author: critical care
documents.body:
Admitted 11/05/2025 to the ICU, discharged 11/14/2025. Hepatology consulted.
Presentation: 61M with CAD (LAD disease on medical therapy), VT with ICD, mitral repair 2023, HTN, T2DM, gout, history of Whipple disease, brought in by his wife after 2 days of increasing weakness and confusion. Three days earlier he had severe chest pain and passed out at home but declined to come in.
On arrival: afebrile, BP 90/60, HR 110. Disoriented to time and place. Jaundiced. Abdomen soft, mild RUQ tenderness, no rebound or guarding.
Labs: Hgb 13.2, WBC 11.0, plt 250; creatinine 1.9 (baseline 1.2); AST 2500, ALT 2200, total bilirubin 3.5, alk phos 120. Troponin elevated. INR peaked 2.1 on 11/06.
ECG: nonspecific ST-T changes.
Diagnoses: late-presenting myocardial infarction with cardiogenic shock; acute (ischemic) liver failure; acute kidney injury.
Course: norepinephrine for 2 days, then weaned. Echo: LVEF 45%, anterior hypokinesis, mitral ring well seated with trace MR. ICD interrogation: no ventricular arrhythmias, no therapies. Once stable, coronary angiography showed occlusion of the LAD at the site of his known lesion; completed infarct, no intervention. Mental status cleared as perfusion improved. Transaminases, bilirubin and INR trended down daily; creatinine 1.3 at discharge.
Discharge medications: START aspirin 81 mg daily. Metformin and lisinopril were held during the stay and RESUMED at discharge. Continue atorvastatin 40 mg, metoprolol succinate 50 mg, allopurinol 300 mg, ibuprofen as needed.
Follow-up: PCP within 1 week with hepatic panel and BMP; cardiology 6-8 weeks.

He'd had chest pain and fainted at home on Sunday and refused to go in; by Wednesday he was weak and confused and she called an ambulance. Told it was a heart attack that dropped his blood pressure and affected his liver and kidneys. Improving, more alert today. Routed to PCP.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
With wife. Summary reviewed: late MI with cardiogenic shock, shock liver and AKI; LAD now occluded, no stent; EF 45%. ICD showed no arrhythmia. Aspirin added; metformin and lisinopril back on at discharge.
Now: tired, walking around the house and short trips outside. No chest pain at rest. Thinking clearly, per wife. Yellow color gone. Appetite returning.
Exam: BP/HR as charted. Sclerae anicteric. Alert, oriented. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. No edema.
Labs today: AST/ALT and bilirubin much lower than at admission, creatinine 1.3.
A/P:
1. Recent MI, shock resolved: aspirin 81 daily, continue metoprolol and atorvastatin 40. Cardiology follow-up in January.
2. Ischemic acute liver injury: improving, recheck hepatic panel in 3 weeks.
3. AKI: creatinine near baseline; BMP with next labs.
Med rec done; list updated.
